extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, researchers, and LaTeX users who need to produce programmatic, publication-quality figures
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and example code for producing high-quality, vectorized mathematical figures using Metapost, including LaTeX integration, unit scaling, loops, color interpolation, and compilation to PDF. Aimed at users who prefer coding graphics over mouse-driven editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer code-generated graphics for precision and repeatability
rubrics_metrics.description: For me it is more natural to use code to generate graphics, if this is possible. Using something like Matlab to draw is possible. The advantage is that once you have a working code which produces what you want, you can easily modify it. If you have an image where you need to repeat things, using loops can facilitate the job (programmers will understand…).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use programmatic drawing when figures require precise placement, many repeated elements, or easy parameter changes. Avoid relying on mouse/touchpad-only editors when you need reproducibility or LaTeX-quality text in figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Metapost for LaTeX-integrated, high-quality vector graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Being used to LaTeX for typesetting math, it was a natural way to draw using code. Most importantly, it allows me to build high quality, vectorized graphics, which are memory efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Metapost when you want vector output (scalable without pixels) and seamless LaTeX math labels; it's suitable for publication figures and thesis illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start by reading and modifying existing Metapost examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The easiest way to start drawing in Metapost is to take a look at some existing codes and modify them. You can find lots of examples in this tutorial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn by copy-modify-run: examine sample .mp files, adapt parameters and code blocks, and iterate. Use online tutorials and example repositories as the first learning resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compile .mp files to PDF with mptopdf or use the online editor
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a linux system, you can compile metapost .mp files to obtain high quality pdfs using the command mptopdf. If not, then you can use the online Metapost editor found here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Linux, prefer mptopdf for local compilation; if you cannot install Metapost, use the online previewer/editor to test and get PDF output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed LaTeX preamble using prologues and verbatimtex for labels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a verbatimtex block and set prologues to enable LaTeX typesetting of labels (btex ... etex), allowing use of LaTeX macros and consistent document fonts in figure labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define a scalable unit variable for consistent sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: u:=25; % 25 = 25bp = 25 PostScript points = 25/72 in wi:=10; he:=7; hoehe:=he*u; breite:=wi*u;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce a unit variable (u) and compute width/height from integer grid counts so you can resize the entire figure by changing u. This makes scaling and layout adjustments easy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pens and pickup to control pen shape and stroke width
rubrics_metrics.description: pickup pensquare scaled 20; ... pickup pencircle scaled 1.5; draw p;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select pen shapes (pensquare, pencircle) and scale them to achieve desired stroke thickness and style. Use pickup before drawing operations to change pen for subsequent draws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulate paths with length, subpath, and point to work on segments
rubrics_metrics.description: p is a path; h=length(p); q := subpath (h*(i-1)/detail,h*i/detail) of p; a:= point c of p;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use length(), subpath(), and point() to split paths, extract segments, and compute positions along a path for fine-grained drawing and placement (e.g., drawing segments with varying attributes or placing labels at specific points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Create color gradients along a path via interpolation in loops
rubrics_metrics.description: for i=1 upto (detail/2): q := subpath ... draw q withcolor (2*i/detail)[a,b]; endfor; (and the mirrored loop for the other half).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpolate between two colors a and b across small subpaths in a loop to produce smooth color transitions along a path. Control 'detail' to adjust granularity of the gradient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use nested loops to draw repeated patterns or grids
rubrics_metrics.description: for i=0 upto 9: for j=-1 upto 8: draw fullcircle scaled 0.3u shifted (i*u, j*u); fill fullcircle scaled 0.3u shifted (i*u, j*u) withcolor white; endfor endfor;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate arrays of repeated elements (grids of disks, tiled patterns) efficiently with nested for loops; shift and scale each element based on loop indices and the unit variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine draw/fill and buildcycle to create complex filled regions
rubrics_metrics.description: %r:= b..((a+b)/2 shifted (.5(a-b) rotated -90))..a; %fill buildcycle(r,q) withcolor .5red; %fill pa withcolor .9999blue;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct compound shapes by building cycles from paths and subpaths, then fill them with color. Use comment/uncomment to experiment with region fills and overlays while developing the figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use labels with btex ... etex and explicit positioning/scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: label ("B",(1/15)*(2.6u,2.7u)) scaled 15 withcolor co ; label ("2" infont defaultfont scaled 8,(4.9u,4.1u)) withcolor co;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place text labels using label with explicit coordinates and scaling; use btex ... etex for LaTeX math and choose fonts/scaling/positioning to match document style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw explicit bounding boxes to control figure extents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw a frame or bounding box to visualize and fix figure extents, which helps when aligning tiled elements or ensuring consistent margins for cropping to PDF.
